contributions.statement: Do not rank or gate Java test generators by mutation score or branch coverage alone, because the tool with the highest mutation score and branch coverage detected 25.6 pp fewer real bugs than one with lower mutation score.
contributions.evidence: §III-B2 Table II on 172 Defects4J single-method bugs: KTester MS 56.72 / BC 74.24 / RBDR 47.09 vs KITE MS 52.90 / RBDR 72.67; MutGen also higher MS, 20.3 pp lower RBDR. Single run, GPT-5.4 only, contamination risk.
relative_to: mutation score as a test-adequacy proxy

contributions.statement: Harden agent-written tests against kill targets built from the project's own historical bug mechanisms (e.g. PIT custom mutators from past defect classes) rather than generic mutants.
contributions.evidence: Table IV: removing synthetic-bug feedback drops RBDR 72.67 to 52.91 (-19.8 pp); recall components contribute ~4 pp each. Uses ~70% more tokens than MutGen; not budget-matched.

reason: Java evaluation on a real-bug metric that shows the usual proxy metrics mislead, plus an ablated mechanism (history-derived kill targets) the team can approximate with PIT. Single model and Defects4J contamination keep it at moderate.
